question:
Consider two distinct positive real numbers 𝑚, 𝑛, with 𝑚> 𝑛.

Let all logarithms be to base 10.

Given:

\[
x = n^{\log_{10}(m)}, \qquad y = m^{\log_{10}(n)}
\]

Take \(\log_{10}\) on both sides.

For \(x\):

\[
\log_{10}(x)=\log_{10}\left(n^{\log_{10}(m)}\right)
\]

Using \(\log(a^b)=b\log(a)\),

\[
\log_{10}(x)=\log_{10}(m)\log_{10}(n)
\]

For \(y\):

\[
\log_{10}(y)=\log_{10}\left(m^{\log_{10}(n)}\right)
\]

\[
\log_{10}(y)=\log_{10}(n)\log_{10}(m)
\]

Thus,

\[
\log_{10}(x)=\log_{10}(y)
\]

Since logarithm is one-to-one,

\[
x=y
\]
